topicName: Data Warehousing Concepts (Data Lakes, Lakehouses, Star/Snowflake Schema)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Data Warehousing Concepts in Modern ETL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern data architecture requires a deep understanding of storage systems and schema designs to build efficient Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipelines. This tutorial covers the foundational concepts of Data Lakes, Data Lakehouses, and dimensional modeling paradigms such as Star and Snowflake schemas."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Data Lakes vs. Data Lakehouses"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Data Lake is a centralized repository that allows you to store all your structured and unstructured data at any scale. While cost-effective, raw data lakes often suffer from a lack of ACID transactions, making reliable ETL pipelines difficult to maintain due to data corruption and concurrency issues."},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Data Lakehouse architecture bridges this gap by combining the best elements of data lakes and data warehouses. Using table storage formats like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, or Apache Hudi, lakehouses add a transactional storage layer on top of low-cost cloud storage."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Dimensional Modeling: Star Schema vs. Snowflake Schema"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once data is extracted and transformed, it is typically loaded into a dimensional model for analytics. The Star Schema is the simplest style of data mart, consisting of a central fact table surrounded by denormalized dimension tables. This structure minimizes joins and optimizes query performance for business intelligence tools."},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Conversely, the Snowflake Schema normalizes dimension tables into multiple related sub-tables. This reduces data redundancy and saves storage space, but it requires more complex SQL JOIN operations during the ETL reporting phase."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Practical ETL Implementation"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is an example of an ETL script using Python and PySpark to read raw data from a data lake, transform it into a dimensional format, and write it out using a modern Lakehouse format (Delta Lake)."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, current_timestamp

# Initialize Spark Session with Delta Lake support
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("ETL_Lakehouse_Pipeline") \
    .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") \
    .config("spark.sparkContext.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog") \
    .getOrCreate()

# 1. Extract raw data from Data Lake
raw_df = spark.read.json("s3://my-data-lake/raw/transactions/")

# 2. Transform: Clean and structure into a Star Schema Dim/Fact format
transformed_fact_df = raw_df.select(
    col("transaction_id").cast("string"),
    col("customer_id").cast("string"),
    col("amount").cast("double"),
    col("date").cast("date")
).withColumn("loaded_at", current_timestamp())

# 3. Load into Data Lakehouse using Delta format
transformed_fact_df.write \
    .format("delta") \
    .mode("append") \
    .save("s3://my-data-lake/lakehouse/fact_transactions")"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Data Lakes for ingestion of raw, multi-structured streaming and batch data."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Adopt Lakehouse storage formats (Delta/Iceberg) to enforce ACID compliance and time travel capabilities."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prefer Star Schemas over Snowflake Schemas for analytical consumption layers to maximize query speed and simplify downstream BI integrations."}]
